name: Virginia Foxx
role: US representative from North Carolina (2005–present), House Rules Committee chair
summary: Foxx advocates limited federal government, market wages, voluntary union membership, school choice and fiscal restraint. Her social policies oppose elective abortion, emphasize parental authority and religious heritage, and retain biological sex classifications.

universal-healthcare.rationale: She expressly rejects universal government healthcare proposals.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: She opposes raising the federal minimum wage to $15, citing employment losses.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: She argues that wages should be determined in the marketplace rather than federally mandated.

public-ownership.rationale: No recorded position found in sources reviewed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In her 2010 tax reform op-ed she puts herself in the "not increasing taxes on anyone" column and later opposed the Biden tax increases; she backs lower rates, not higher taxes on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: She criticizes unions for prioritizing partisan politics over worker representation, while supporting voluntary membership.

property-fundamental.rationale: Her 2005 column calls the Kelo eminent-domain ruling an unconstitutional contradiction of the ideals of liberty and property rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: She seeks systematic repeal of workplace regulations and favors free enterprise.

cut-welfare.rationale: She says expanded anti-poverty programs "put more people in dependency" and that the CSBG has become a welfare program that keeps people in poverty, and she voted for the 2013 SNAP cuts and work rules; she also says a safety net for those truly in need should stay.

empower-police-military.rationale: She introduced the Qualified Immunity Act to codify protection for police and criticised cuts to the defense authorization topline; she rejects calls to defund police.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: She voted against federal recognition protections in the Respect for Marriage Act (December 2022).

abortion-legal.rationale: She supports protecting life from conception and legislation restricting elective abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: She urges preserving Judeo-Christian public heritage and rejects excluding religious convictions from public debate.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: No recorded position found in sources reviewed.

free-trade.rationale: She voted for trade promotion authority because trade supports North Carolina jobs, and she backed reforms favouring free trade while seeking accountability from partners.

notes:
No inference used. Reviewed official issue pages, labor and education speeches, campaign platform, immigration proposals and marriage vote. Border enforcement is not equated with reducing all immigration; opposition to trans participation in women’s sports is not expanded into an answer about every form of gender-identity recognition. Full committee opening statements were downloaded and searched.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 24 answers taken from it, 21 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass (Sonnet) from about 980 foxx.house.gov press releases and op-eds (2005-2026) and about 1,050 edworkforce.house.gov releases, searched by theme: economy, taxes, trade, welfare, labor, health, education, guns, courts and separation of powers, elections, abortion and marriage, race and gender, immigration, foreign policy (UN, ICC, Israel, Ukraine, Iran, China). Searched without finding a position: surveillance (FISA votes are mixed), drugs, death penalty, sentencing, encryption and AI, religion in schools, LGBT military service, Indigenous and language questions, populist or radical-left statements. Government-record answers rest on her own statements or bills she introduced or voted on; votes alone were treated as medium at most. The Bioguide page was blocked by a bot wall and was not used.
